source.title: Impact of Training Set Size on the Ability of Deep Neural Networks to Deal with Omission Noise
source.authors: Jonas Gütter; Anna M. Kruspe; Xiao-Xia Zhu; Julia Niebling

record.file_problem: Full article text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests omission noise and training-set size for building segmentation, extending noisy-label robustness findings to a remote-sensing setting. It does not test random label assignments as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports clean-validation outcomes as omission noise varies. This is a distinct noise type from randomly assigned labels. Training-set fit error is not reported, and shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-input tests are absent. Figure-only metric values are not reconstructed. Cited findings about memorizing label noise and learning clean labels first are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures clean-validation segmentation performance after randomly omitting whole building annotations. This creates asymmetric building-to-background corruption, not completely random labels. It reports neither training-set fit nor learning dynamics separating clean and noisy labels. Memorization and clean-label-first learning are cited findings; the proposed memorization explanation for small datasets is speculative.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that larger training sets improve omission-noise robustness in this setup, although most relative metric declines are similar and the improvement is modest. Very small sets generalize poorly; building precision is comparatively robust up to omission level 0.8, with small-set exceptions described in the results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DeepLabV3+ on building-segmentation images with whole-building omission noise; studies training-set size and clean-validation metrics rather than fitting completely random labels or measuring training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-set size and omission-noise level affect reported outcomes. Small sets of 100, 500, and 1,000 images perform poorly even without added noise; relative building-class metrics generally show greater vulnerability for smaller sets. Background-class IoU has no clear size ordering, and background recall's relative ordering is reversed.

fits_no_version.finding: DeepLabV3+ validation performance depends on training-set size and whole-building omission noise. Larger sets generally improve building-metric robustness; very small sets perform poorly even without noise. Building precision remains comparatively robust through omission level 0.8, with exceptions for the smallest sets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-set size affects robustness to asymmetric omission noise in building segmentation, with effects depending on the evaluation metric.

record.problems: The results concern omission noise rather than randomly assigned labels. Training error is not reported. Precise values are presented in figures and were not transcribed here; the study reports standard deviations across 10 repetitions. The authors note that the smallest training sizes cannot learn reasonable patterns, limiting practical interpretation of their noise vulnerability.
record.rows_left_out: Many figure-only results across metrics, noise levels, and all six training-set sizes are not separately extracted due to the 60-row cap. Rows prioritize building-class IoU at noise levels 0 and 1, the text-described building precision qualification, and pixelwise-accuracy behavior by size. Omitted measurements appear in Figures 2, 4–6.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without architecture or hyperparameter changes.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across random-label corruption levels and steadily increasing test error toward chance. Omission-noise validation curves do not establish this conjunction.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing regularization.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noise; separate clean-label and noisy-label learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: At full omission, validation accuracy approaches the background-class prevalence of 0.928 through all-background prediction; this is not chance performance under random labels. No omitted result in the supplied text directly tests V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random label assignments, zero or near-zero training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and convergence rate as the fraction of corrupted labels rises.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Randomly corrupted labels, perfect training-set fit across corruption levels, and the claimed gradual rise in test error toward chance.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, and whether those labels are learned differently over training.

rows.size_stated: not stated (six training-set sizes: 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000, 10,000, and 11,080 images)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with different omission-noise levels and evaluated on a clean validation set.
rows.measure: Precision of the building class on the clean validation set.
rows.value: The models are described as robust against label noise up to a noise level of 0.8.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation across 10 repetitions is shown in the figures.
rows.note: The authors qualify that only models trained on the smallest dataset sizes show a clear decrease at low and medium noise levels; the text does not report separate exact values by size.
rows.check: Change partial to cannot_determine relative to the claim versions. Building precision under omission noise measures a different outcome. This pooled row also combines dataset sizes with different precision responses; the smallest sizes show deterioration and high variability.

rows.check: Change partial to cannot_determine relative to the claim versions. Nearly constant validation accuracy reflects background-biased predictions, not partial evidence for random-label fitting or memorization dynamics.
